pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these words is a noun? (1 mark)
   A. slowly
   B. millet
   C. tasty
   D. boil

2. What does reading for information mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading only for fun
   B. Reading the page numbers
   C. Reading to learn something new
   D. Reading without understanding

3. What can a weather forecast tell us? (1 mark)
   A. How old we are
   B. Who will win a race
   C. What the weather will be like
   D. What we will eat

4. What should a reader do at a full stop? (1 mark)
   A. Skip a line
   B. Shout
   C. Turn the page
   D. Pause briefly

5. Which word must begin with a capital letter in the middle of a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Monday
   B. weather
   C. cloud
   D. morning

6. Why do we use punctuation marks? (1 mark)
   A. To make writing clear
   B. To use up ink
   C. To make pages heavy
   D. To hide meaning

7. What is the guessing language game with verbs? (1 mark)
   A. Pupils write verbs on the board silently
   B. Pupils sing nouns
   C. Pupils act a verb and others guess it
   D. Pupils read a book

8. Why do we put ideas in order? (1 mark)
   A. So the reader can follow them
   B. To use more words
   C. To make the story shorter
   D. To confuse the reader

9. What is an oral narrative? (1 mark)
   A. A story kept secret
   B. A drawing
   C. A story told aloud
   D. A written test

10. What can wall charts of similes and metaphors help with? (1 mark)
   A. Gallery walks and learning from each other
   B. Running
   C. Cooking
   D. Sleeping

11. What is a good rule for handling library books? (1 mark)
   A. Turn pages gently and return them on time
   B. Leave them outside
   C. Fold the corners
   D. Write in them

12. Why do many readers read silently? (1 mark)
   A. It is illegal to read aloud
   B. Books cannot be read aloud
   C. It is boring
   D. It is fast and does not disturb others

13. What is profit? (1 mark)
   A. Money left after paying the cost
   B. A bill
   C. A kind of shop
   D. Money spent

14. Which preposition needs two things to make sense? (1 mark)
   A. in
   B. under
   C. on
   D. between

15. What does pace mean when reading a poem? (1 mark)
   A. How loud you read
   B. How fast or slow you read
   C. How many words rhyme
   D. How long the poem is

16. Which element tells where and when a story happens? (1 mark)
   A. Ending
   B. Title
   C. Character
   D. Setting

17. What is a debate? (1 mark)
   A. A song
   B. A discussion in which two sides give opposite views with reasons
   C. A game of football
   D. A kind of poem

18. In the kite passage, what went wrong? (1 mark)
   A. The kite flew away forever
   B. The children fell
   C. The string broke
   D. The wind stopped

19. Which adjective describes shape? (1 mark)
   A. heavy
   B. red
   C. round
   D. loud

20. What should you not do with an advert that asks for money from strangers? (1 mark)
   A. Ask an adult
   B. Read it carefully
   C. Send money without asking an adult
   D. Check the facts

21. What should a newsreader do? (1 mark)
   A. Mumble
   B. Shout
   C. Speak clearly at a steady pace
   D. Skip words

22. What should you do first before filling a form? (1 mark)
   A. Fold it
   B. Fill any box
   C. Read all the instructions
   D. Sign

23. Which is a common field on a form? (1 mark)
   A. The number of windows
   B. Name
   C. Colour of the wall
   D. Type of soil

24. What does a signature show? (1 mark)
   A. Your own handwriting of your name confirming the information
   B. The paper size
   C. The colour of a pen
   D. The price of a form

25. Which of these is an action verb? (1 mark)
   A. very
   B. the
   C. lead
   D. is

26. What are images in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Maps
   B. Photographs
   C. Diagrams
   D. Words that make pictures in the mind

27. What are non-verbal cues in a performance? (1 mark)
   A. Gestures and facial expressions
   B. Loud shouting
   C. Written words
   D. Music only

28. What is an instruction chart? (1 mark)
   A. A list of animals
   B. A story chart
   C. A poster showing steps for a task
   D. A drawing of a house

29. Why do leaders need to give clear instructions? (1 mark)
   A. To waste time
   B. To confuse people
   C. So people know exactly what to do
   D. To make noise

30. Which is the correct order for washing hands? (1 mark)
   A. Soap, dry, wet, rinse
   B. Rinse, dry, wet, soap
   C. Dry, wet, soap, rinse
   D. Wet, rub soap, rinse, dry

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. A picture shows a girl beside a thin dog under a tree with an empty bowl. Write a story plan and a four-sentence story. (5 marks)

32. Explain why sequencing ideas is important in writing. (3 marks)

33. Write the verbs in this instruction: Close the door and sit down. (2 marks)

34. Explain what a subject and a predicate are, then write one sentence and divide it. (5 marks)

35. Give three rules for punctuating a dialogue. (3 marks)

36. Describe how a group can read a text aloud together and give feedback. (4 marks)

37. Give two adjectives to describe a school bag in an advert. (2 marks)

38. Play the role of the soloist in a singing game. Write three short instructions you would sing and say what the group should do for each. (5 marks)

39. Read: Fire can be dangerous. Never play with matches. Ask an adult to light the stove. If your clothes catch fire, stop, drop and roll. State the main idea and list three details. (5 marks)

40. Describe how a panel discussion is organised. (4 marks)

41. Explain what a form is. (2 marks)

42. Pick out the nouns in this song line: We roast the maize and boil the beans. (3 marks)

43. Describe what a written dialogue shows. (2 marks)

44. List three ways of reading with expression. (3 marks)

45. Explain what an interjection is and give two examples. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — millet
   Millet is a grain, so it names a thing. The others are an action, a describing word and an adverb.

2. C — Reading to learn something new
   We read for information to find facts and learn.

3. C — What the weather will be like
   A forecast predicts the weather.

4. D — Pause briefly
   Full stops tell us to pause.

5. A — Monday
   Days of the week begin with capital letters.

6. A — To make writing clear
   Punctuation helps readers understand.

7. C — Pupils act a verb and others guess it
   Acting helps everyone connect verbs with actions.

8. A — So the reader can follow them
   Order makes writing clear.

9. C — A story told aloud
   Oral narratives are spoken stories.

10. A — Gallery walks and learning from each other
   Charts display the sayings for review.

11. A — Turn pages gently and return them on time
   Good care keeps books usable for others.

12. D — It is fast and does not disturb others
   Silent reading is quiet and lets you think.

13. A — Money left after paying the cost
   Profit is gain after costs.

14. D — between
   Between means with something on each side.

15. B — How fast or slow you read
   Pace is speed.

16. D — Setting
   Setting means place and time.

17. B — A discussion in which two sides give opposite views with reasons
   A debate is an organised argument of a motion.

18. C — The string broke
   The string broke and the kite fell.

19. C — round
   Round describes shape.

20. C — Send money without asking an adult
   Never send money to strangers.

21. C — Speak clearly at a steady pace
   Clear speech helps listeners.

22. C — Read all the instructions
   Reading first prevents mistakes.

23. B — Name
   Name is a common field.

24. A — Your own handwriting of your name confirming the information
   A signature confirms you agree.

25. C — lead
   Lead shows action.

26. D — Words that make pictures in the mind
   Images are word pictures.

27. A — Gestures and facial expressions
   Non-verbal cues are actions without words.

28. C — A poster showing steps for a task
   It shows steps in order.

29. C — So people know exactly what to do
   Clear instructions get work done safely.

30. D — Wet, rub soap, rinse, dry
   This is the logical order.

SECTION B
----
31. (5 marks)
   Answer: A plan with title, characters, setting, problem and ending, followed by four sentences that show the girl helping the dog and end with a lesson.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for characters, setting and problem, and two marks for a clear four-sentence story.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: It helps the reader follow the ideas, avoids confusion and makes writing logical.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each valid point.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: close, sit
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb.

34. (5 marks)
   Answer: The subject is who or what the sentence is about and the predicate says what the subject does. Example: The girl (subject) counts the coins (predicate).
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the two meanings, one for a sentence, and two marks for the correct division.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name then colon, capital letter to begin the words, end with a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark, a new line for each speaker.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, help each other with hard words, take turns to read, then listen to the group and give one good point and one point to improve in a kind way.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct parts.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: strong, big, red, light, new (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each adjective.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three clear instructions with matching actions, for example Clap two times (the group claps twice), Stir the pot (the group pretends to stir), Turn around (the group turns).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each clear instruction and one mark for each matching response, with a total of five marks for three well matched pairs and correct listening steps.

39. (5 marks)
   Answer: Main idea: Fire is dangerous and needs care. Details: never play with matches, ask an adult to light the stove, stop drop and roll.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the main idea and one mark for each of three details.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a topic, a moderator and panel members, panel members give opinions in turn, the audience asks questions, the moderator summarises.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: A form is a page with spaces where people write information in an organised way.
   Working / marking points: One mark for a page with spaces and one for collecting information.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: maize and beans (and we is a pronoun, not a noun)
   Working / marking points: One mark for maize, one mark for beans, and one mark for not including roast or boil, which are actions.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people written to show what each speaker says.
   Working / marking points: One mark for conversation and one for showing speakers' words.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Change loudness, change speed, pause at punctuation, use different voices for characters, use face and hands.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: An interjection is a short word or sound showing sudden feeling, for example Wow and Ouch.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for two examples.
